title: Autonomy rules are not service
summary: A technology-readiness map connecting policy, reporting, recalls, vehicle and passenger-service authority, operating exposure, aviation approvals, local systems, and measured service outcomes.
map_question: How do mobility and aviation policy records become certified, locally authorized, safety-evidenced autonomous service?
interpretation_boundary: The map now supports a named road passenger-service authorization and measured testing exposure. It does not prove actual trip volume, comparative safety, accessibility, cost, local outcomes, eVTOL certification, or aviation service.

nodes.label: Federal policy and program design
nodes.note: The AV Framework and AV STEP proposal define possible federal directions without proving final implementation.

nodes.label: Crash reporting and defect evidence
nodes.note: NHTSA's amended SGO supplies a reporting rail with explicit data limitations.

nodes.label: Weather-related ADS recall
nodes.note: A specific recall exposes software, map, weather, operating-scope, and remedy dependencies.

nodes.label: Powered-lift operating rule
nodes.note: FAA has completed one pilot and operating-rule layer while aircraft and operator approvals remain separate.

nodes.label: eVTOL pilot selections
nodes.note: Eight selected proposals create a test lane but do not establish sites, flights, safety results, or service.

nodes.label: Road passenger-service authority
nodes.note: CPUC authorizes fared Waymo driverless passenger service in specified California geographies.

nodes.label: Road operating exposure
nodes.note: DMV testing miles provide measured exposure with scope and comparison limits.

nodes.note: Type, production, exemption, operator, route, and operational-design-domain approvals remain system-specific.

nodes.label: Local infrastructure and permission
nodes.note: FTFN still needs sites, roads, airspace, vertiports, charging, emergency processes, insurance, weather, noise, and community records.

nodes.label: Operating service and outcomes
nodes.note: Flights or trips, availability, safety, disruptions, costs, ridership, service area, and enforcement establish operation and scale.

what_this_map_supports: A named road carrier has effective authority for fared driverless passenger service in specified California geographies.
California testing-mile reports and NHTSA crash reporting provide operating-exposure and safety-oversight rails with explicit limits.
Road passenger-service authority and powered-lift aviation remain separate legal and operating systems.
what_this_map_does_not_prove: It does not prove trip volume, comparative safety, service quality, accessibility, cost, local acceptance, or scale.
It does not treat testing miles as passenger-service trips.
It does not transfer road authorization into aircraft, operator, route, site, or aviation-service approval.
